published_failure_contract: BaseTestCase annotates the static wireMockRule field with both @ClassRule and @Rule. JUnit 4.11 validates every @Rule member as non-static and rejects the class before executing tests.

source_isolation.evidence: JUnit commit b4f0afa639b42fa551fdcb26d9c1855ae4d778cf is an ancestor of r4.11 but not r4.10. It changes RuleFieldValidator to emit 'must not be static' for static @Rule fields and adds a matching regression test.

a1_input.evidence: The FSE package records the 4.10 to 4.11 failure but omits the exact target revision. The offending field first appears in commit 5d8f77a34d835c3f23b91a74b57fc9c1c08d9c7d and remains unchanged in every reachable version of BaseTestCase.

target_history.evidence: All 152 commits reachable from remote refs and all five unique BaseTestCase blobs were inspected. Every blob retains both @ClassRule and @Rule on the static field. The 2021 JUnit 4.13.1 upgrade also retains the invalid annotation combination.

stop_reason: The source mechanism is exact, but the complete target history contains no maintainer-authored repair. Removing @Rule now would be a dataset-author patch, not historical A2.

published_failure_contract: CqlTestEnvironment declares cqlUnit as a static @Rule. JUnit 4.11 rejects the test class during rule validation with the exact published message.

source_isolation.evidence: JUnit commit b4f0afa639b42fa551fdcb26d9c1855ae4d778cf is an ancestor of r4.11 but not r4.10 and adds the exact static-@Rule rejection.

a1_input.evidence: The FSE package records the failure after replacing JUnit 4.10 with 4.11 but omits the exact target revision.

target_history.evidence: All 253 commits reachable from remote refs were inspected. All five unique CqlTestEnvironment blobs and all three unique SalesTopology blobs keep a static @Rule, no reachable source introduces @ClassRule, and all 81 unique POM blobs continue to declare JUnit 4.10 rather than 4.11.

stop_reason: The source mechanism is exact, but the target never adopted JUnit 4.11 and contains no maintainer repair for the static rule contract.

published_failure_contract: The target timing test asserts that a waiting thread returns in less than ten seconds after latch.reset(). The published run observes a false target-side condition and reports AssertionError through JUnit Assert.

source_isolation.evidence: The failing expression is target code assertTrue(t.result < TimeUnit.SECONDS.toNanos(10)). JUnit's assertTrue contract remains the same across 4.10 and 4.11; the 4.11 stack line is only where the false condition is surfaced. No release commit was found that explains why the target thread result reached the timeout.

a1_input.evidence: The FSE package records one failing replacement run but omits the exact target revision and repetitions needed to distinguish a timing flake.

target_history.evidence: All 67 commits reachable from remote refs and the sole unique blob of DefaultRetryLatch_tryAwaitTest were inspected. The test assertion is unchanged from the initial commit, and no POM blob adopts JUnit 4.11.

stop_reason: Neither an exact JUnit source mechanism nor a maintainer recovery exists. Replaying a single timing failure cannot establish a causal cross-repository relation.
